messages:
maria: Heads-up — I found ~120 accounts still have `team:eng-admins` privileges even though the SCIM group was deleted from Okta yesterday. Suspect permission drift from manual grants or a missed deprovision event.

samir: Can you paste the provisioning webhook / SCIM logs? Did the delete event reach our provisioner?

maria: Pasting the relevant tail of scim-provisioner logs:```
2026-03-18T22:03:11Z INFO received event DELETE group id=okta|00gA..
2026-03-18T22:03:11Z INFO enqueue delta job group-delete group_id=00gA..
2026-03-18T22:03:12Z WARN delta-processor batch timeout=30s for group-delete id=00gA..
2026-03-18T22:03:12Z ERROR delta-processor skipped membership deletes 120 users (reason: batch_timeout)
2026-03-18T22:03:12Z INFO job-scheduler retrying 2/3 backoff=5m
```

kevin: That batch timeout matches the new per-batch KMS call change we deployed last week (we added envelope decryption per membership). If the decrypts are slow it can cause the batch to exceed timeout and skip items.

irene: Audit logs show a handful of manual grants too: `admin-console` actor `mary-cs` on 2026-03-18T21:45 — looks like support escalated some users before group was removed. So two causes: manual grants + skipped SCIM deletes.

maria: Ugh. So drifting permissions remained because (A) the delta job skipped due to timeout, and (B) support gave manual grants that are independent of SCIM mapping. We need a short remediation plan.

kevin: Quick checks: run SQL to enumerate suspected shadow memberships:```sql
SELECT u.id, u.email, r.role, r.grant_source
FROM user_roles r
JOIN users u ON u.id = r.user_id
WHERE r.role = 'eng-admin' AND (r.grant_source = 'manual' OR r.scim_group_id IS NULL)
ORDER BY u.email;
```
(maria: I ran a dry-run and exported ~120 rows).

irene: For root cause: the KMS client had a fallback to slow HSM path after rotate; we should revert that path for provisioning to avoid per-member crypto. Suggest switching to bulk-envelopes for now.

maria: Proposed remediation steps: 1) run `scim-reconcile --dry-run --filter group=eng-admins` to compare SCIM source vs DB (already did). 2) enable `enforce_scim_revocation=true` feature flag for the provisioning service so manual grants that conflict with SCIM are flagged (not auto-removed) and create tickets. 3) run one-off `scim-revoke` job to remove non-exempt manual grants after approvals. 4) patch delta processor to use bulk decrypt and increase batch timeout + add faster circuit-breaker logging. 5) notify affected teams and post-mortem.

samir: Can we do the revoke as a canary? e.g., run against 10 users then 100. Need on-call in case of false positives.

kevin: KMS note — if we revoke keys or change KMS policies, the provisioning job might fail while decrypting cached envelopes. We should not rotate keys until reconciliation is complete. Also ensure the revoke job runs with an elevated service principal that bypasses per-member decrypts (reads bulk-envelopes).

devsec-bot: Created issue SEC-3412: "scim delta batch timeout -> shadow memberships" and linked runbook.

deploy-bot: Ran dry-run: `/jobs/run scim-reconcile --env=prod --group=eng-admins --dry-run` output: `dry-run: 120 revokes detected, 0 errors`

maria: OK I'm scheduling the actual revoke for 2026-03-19 03:00 UTC as a canary of 25 users first. Who can be on-call to monitor?

irene: I can stay on for the canary and watch KMS + provisioner logs.

kevin: I'll be available for rollback and to patch the decrypt path if we see batch timeouts.

samir: I'll notify the support team to freeze manual grants for the next 24h and open a communication to affected product leads.

maria: Thanks everyone. Postmortem draft will go to #postmortems after the canary. :thumbsup:

kevin: One actionable follow-up — increase `delta_processor.batch_timeout` to 2m and add a metric `scim.delta.skipped_members` so we alert on >5 in 1h.

maria: Agreed. I'll add those changes to the PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioner/pull/492

devsec-bot: Reminder: label SEC-3412 with `high-priority` and attach audit export.

maria: Final: canary at 03:00 UTC, post-cana ry review at 04:00 UTC. I'll update thread with results.
